question.text: Jordan wants to paint the outside of his home. Using $2$ gallons of paint, he was able to paint $450$ square feet of the surface. There is a proportional relationship between the volume of paint $x$ (in gallons) that Jordan uses and the area $y$ (in square feet) he paints. What is the equation that represents the relationship between $x$ and $y?$
question.explanation:
Every proportional relationship takes the form $y=kx,$ where $k$ is the constant of proportionality.

We are told that Jordan painted $y=450$ square feet using $x=2$ gallons of paint.

We can find the constant of proportionality by computing the ratio of the $y$-value to the $x$-value, as follows:

\[ k = \dfrac{y}{x} = \dfrac{450}{2} = 225\]

Therefore, the equation is

\[ y = 225 x. \]

example.title: Identifying the Equation of a Proportional Relationship

question.text: Let $b$ be directly proportional to $g.$ Given that $b=98$ when $g=-7$, find the value of $b$ when $g=\dfrac{31}{7}.$
question.explanation:
Since $b$ varies directly with $g,$ we use the equation

\[ b = kg. \]

We are told that $b=98$ when $g=-7.$ We substitute this data into the equation to find $k\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} 98 &= k \cdot (-7) \\[5pt] \dfrac{98}{(-7)} &= k \\[5pt] -14 &= k \end{align*}

So, the direct variation equation is given by \[ b=-14g. \]

Finally, substituting the value of $g=\dfrac{31}{7}$ into this equation gives \begin{align*} b &= -14 \cdot \dfrac{31}{7} \\[5pt] &= -2 \cdot 31\\[5pt] & = -62. \end{align*}

question.text: Suppose $v$ is directly proportional to $u.$ Given that $v=-12$ when $u=3$, find the value of $v$ when $u=5.$
question.explanation:
Since $v$ varies directly with $u,$ we use the equation

\[ v = ku. \]

We are told that $v=-12$ when $u=3.$ We substitute this data into the equation to find $k\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} -12 &= k \cdot 3 \\[5pt] \dfrac{(-12)}{3} &= k \\[5pt] -4 &= k \end{align*}

So, the direct variation equation is given by \[ v=-4u. \]

Finally, substituting the value of $u=5$ into this equation gives \begin{align*} v &= -4 \cdot 5 = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-20}. \end{align*}
